genuineNewConclusion: The old c65 gate can remain removed, but that does not establish an empty complete Mathematics set. Both mandatory current Physics cases require independent reading of quantitative axes, their scales and units. Propose the complete existing Math80 axis/scale/unit competence as a direct prerequisite for this exact profile, with the general time-position modeling, experimental plan, fit/uncertainty judgment and physical sign/model interpretation learned and assessed within Physics.
directness: Mastery of e4b38061 or ce431132 does not confer Math80 mastery. The new goal itself graphically analyzes fresh data, so its required axis/scale/unit operation must be checked directly even if either Physics predecessor is mastered.

wholePhysicsCaseSolutions.safePlan: Use a supervised short drop and a camera or position sensor with calibrated position/time scales; state testable approximately-constant-acceleration question, vary observation time, control object, release state, initial height and camera alignment. Supplied data still require the plan explanation. Never perform an unsafe real drop in this review.
wholePhysicsCaseSolutions.model: Upward y positive: y=1.8+0.4t-4.9t^2 m for t in seconds; acceleration -9.8m/s². Measured y,t are distinct from inferred coefficient and g.
wholePhysicsCaseSolutions.graphicalInference: Plot residual y-y0-v0*t against t² with labelled quantities/units; the slope is -4.9m/s², hence g=9.8m/s². An explicitly synthetic graphical envelope of slopes[-5.0,-4.8] gives g in[9.6,10.0]m/s²; this is a declared interval rule, not an invented universal statistical uncertainty estimator.
wholePhysicsCaseSolutions.axisUnitTransfer: If t² ticks are in0.01s² and residual ticks are in cm, numeric display slope is -4.9cm per0.01s², physically -4.9m/s². Ignoring labels or interpreting these as categorical ticks yields a false g. No arbitrary function evaluation at negative time is necessary.
wholePhysicsCaseSolutions.retainedDuties: Fit/model limitation, initial height and velocity, orientation/sign, justified uncertainty and safe testable plan remain required.

wholePhysicsCaseSolutions.interpretation: Ball distance/t² stays4.9m/s². Filter values decrease over time and depart beyond a suitable stated measurement envelope, so a single constant-g no-drag law fails for that broad object. The local gravitational field need not differ. Compare like coordinate/time quantities and their axes before attributing the discrepancy to drag.
wholePhysicsCaseSolutions.modelOnlyGeneratorBoundary: The log(cosh) function is used only by this author to synthesize a plausible drag table, never supplied as a required learner calculation or new mathematical prerequisite.
wholePhysicsCaseSolutions.massBoundary: For different compact masses in the no-drag model, acceleration is equal, weight m*g differs; speed and force units remain distinct.
wholePhysicsCaseSolutions.newPlanningRequirement: Even the supplied-data option includes the safe controlled-plan explanation; it adds experimental design and scale choice, not an arbitrary new function course.
